fr: Je coupe les oignons pour la soupe.
en: I cut the onions for the soup.
ipa: /ʒə kup lez‿ɔɲɔ̃ puʁ la sup/
notes: The liaison between les and oignons adds a z sound that is easy to miss when writing.

fr: Elle épluche les carottes avec un couteau.
en: She peels the carrots with a knife.
ipa: /ɛl eplyʃ le kaʁɔt avɛk œ̃ kuto/
notes: The plural s on carottes is completely silent, so listen for les to know it is plural.

fr: Nous mangeons du pain frais chaque matin.
en: We eat fresh bread every morning.
ipa: /nu mɑ̃ʒɔ̃ dy pɛ̃ fʁɛ ʃak matɛ̃/
notes: Pain and matin both end in the nasal vowel in, which has no separate n sound to write out.

fr: Il boit un café sans sucre.
en: He drinks coffee without sugar.
ipa: /il bwa œ̃ kafe sɑ̃ sykʁ/
notes: Sans sounds exactly like sang and cent, so rely on meaning to spell it correctly.

fr: Tu manges une pomme à midi.
en: You eat an apple at noon.
ipa: /ty mɑ̃ʒ yn pɔm a midi/
notes: The preposition à sounds identical to the verb form a, but only one has an accent.

fr: Les enfants aiment les pâtes au fromage.
en: The children like pasta with cheese.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ ɛm le pat o fʁɔmaʒ/
notes: Les enfants is joined by a z liaison that must not be forgotten in writing.

fr: Le chef prépare un plat délicieux.
en: The chef prepares a delicious dish.
ipa: /lə ʃɛf pʁepaʁ œ̃ pla delisjø/
notes: The final t of plat is never pronounced, which often leads learners to drop it in spelling too.

fr: Nous achetons des ananas au marché.
en: We buy pineapples at the market.
ipa: /nuz‿aʃtɔ̃ dez‿anana o maʁʃe/
notes: Des ananas carries a z liaison from des that links smoothly into the vowel of ananas.

fr: Elle met un peu de sel dans la soupe.
en: She puts a little salt in the soup.
ipa: /ɛl mɛ œ̃ pø də sɛl dɑ̃ la sup/
notes: The verb met and the noun mets, meaning a dish, sound the same, so context decides the spelling.

fr: Il coupe le pain en tranches fines.
en: He cuts the bread into thin slices.
ipa: /il kup lə pɛ̃ ɑ̃ tʁɑ̃ʃ fin/
notes: En and tranches both use nasal vowels that have no audible n or m to copy down.

fr: Je fais cuire le riz dans l'eau chaude.
en: I cook the rice in hot water.
ipa: /ʒə fɛ kɥiʁ lə ʁi dɑ̃ lo ʃod/
notes: La eau is impossible to say, so la elides to l' before the vowel of eau.

fr: Les oeufs sont dans le réfrigérateur.
en: The eggs are in the refrigerator.
ipa: /lez‿ø sɔ̃ dɑ̃ lə ʁefʁiʒeʁatœʁ/
notes: Unlike singular un oeuf where the f is heard, the f and s of plural oeufs both stay silent.

fr: Tu bois de l'eau avec ton repas.
en: You drink water with your meal.
ipa: /ty bwa də lo avɛk tɔ̃ ʁəpa/
notes: De drops its e before the vowel in eau, becoming de l'eau.

fr: Nous préparons le dîner ensemble ce soir.
en: We are preparing dinner together tonight.
ipa: /nu pʁepaʁɔ̃ lə dine ɑ̃sɑ̃bl sə swaʁ/
notes: Dîner keeps a circumflex accent on the i even though it does not change the sound.

fr: Elle achète des fruits frais tous les jours.
en: She buys fresh fruit every day.
ipa: /ɛl aʃɛt de fʁɥi fʁɛ tu le ʒuʁ/
notes: Before a consonant, tous drops its final s sound, unlike when it stands alone.

fr: Il mélange la farine et les oeufs frais.
en: He mixes the flour and the fresh eggs.
ipa: /il melɑ̃ʒ la faʁin e lez‿ø fʁɛ/
notes: Les oeufs needs the z liaison from les even though oeufs itself starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Les tomates sont mûres et rouges.
en: The tomatoes are ripe and red.
ipa: /le tɔmat sɔ̃ myʁ e ʁuʒ/
notes: Sont is a homophone of son, so only the sentence meaning tells them apart.

fr: Je goûte la sauce avant de servir.
en: I taste the sauce before serving.
ipa: /ʒə gut la sos avɑ̃ də sɛʁviʁ/
notes: Goûte keeps its circumflex accent on the u, a spelling detail invisible in speech.

fr: Vous mangez du poulet rôti ce soir.
en: You are eating roast chicken tonight.
ipa: /vu mɑ̃ʒe dy pulɛ ʁoti sə swaʁ/
notes: The final t of poulet is always silent, like most words ending in -et.

fr: Elle lave les fraises dans l'évier.
en: She washes the strawberries in the sink.
ipa: /ɛl lav le fʁɛz dɑ̃ levje/
notes: La évier cannot be said aloud, so la becomes l' before the vowel.

fr: Il ajoute du poivre sur la viande.
en: He adds pepper to the meat.
ipa: /il aʒut dy pwavʁ syʁ la vjɑ̃d/
notes: Sur, meaning on, and sûr, meaning certain, sound identical, only the accent tells them apart in writing.

fr: Nous cuisinons ensemble le dimanche matin.
en: We cook together on Sunday morning.
ipa: /nu kɥizinɔ̃ ɑ̃sɑ̃bl lə dimɑ̃ʃ matɛ̃/
notes: Ensemble and dimanche both hide nasal vowels with no separate n or m sound.

fr: Ils mangent des légumes verts chaque soir.
en: They eat green vegetables every evening.
ipa: /il mɑ̃ʒ de legym vɛʁ ʃak swaʁ/
notes: Mangent sounds exactly like the singular mange, so only the subject ils signals the plural.

fr: Je prends deux oeufs pour l'omelette.
en: I take two eggs for the omelette.
ipa: /ʒə pʁɑ̃ døz‿ø puʁ lɔmlɛt/
notes: La omelette is not possible to pronounce, so it becomes l'omelette.

fr: Le pain sent bon dans la cuisine.
en: The bread smells good in the kitchen.
ipa: /lə pɛ̃ sɑ̃ bɔ̃ dɑ̃ la kɥizin/
notes: Pain, sent and bon all rely on nasal vowels that leave no separate letter to hear.

fr: Elle sert la soupe très chaude.
en: She serves the soup very hot.
ipa: /ɛl sɛʁ la sup tʁɛ ʃod/
notes: The t at the end of sert is silent, so it is easy to forget when spelling the verb.

fr: Il verse l'huile dans la poêle.
en: He pours the oil into the pan.
ipa: /il vɛʁs lɥil dɑ̃ la pwal/
notes: La huile is never said, la elides to l' before this vowel sound.

fr: Je ne mange pas de fromage.
en: I do not eat cheese.
ipa: /ʒə nə mɑ̃ʒ pa də fʁɔmaʒ/
notes: The mute e in je and ne is barely heard, so both words are easy to run together when writing.

fr: Elle achète du beurre frais pour la tarte.
en: She buys fresh butter for the pie.
ipa: /ɛl aʃɛt dy bœʁ fʁɛ puʁ la taʁt/
notes: Achète needs a grave accent on the e to keep the open sound, unlike acheter.

fr: Nous buvons un jus de fruits ensemble.
en: We drink a fruit juice together.
ipa: /nu byvɔ̃ œ̃ ʒy də fʁɥi ɑ̃sɑ̃bl/
notes: Un and ensemble both carry nasal vowels with no separate consonant sound to spell.

fr: Les invités arrivent pour le déjeuner.
en: The guests arrive for lunch.
ipa: /lez‿ɛ̃vite aʁiv puʁ lə deʒøne/
notes: Les invités is joined by a z liaison since invités starts with a vowel sound.

fr: Je range les assiettes dans le placard.
en: I put the plates away in the cupboard.
ipa: /ʒə ʁɑ̃ʒ lez‿asjɛt dɑ̃ lə plakaʁ/
notes: Les assiettes links with a z sound from les before the vowel of assiettes.

fr: Elle choisit un gâteau au chocolat.
en: She chooses a chocolate cake.
ipa: /ɛl ʃwazi œ̃ gato o ʃɔkɔla/
notes: Gâteau keeps its circumflex accent on the a, a silent spelling clue.

fr: Tu manges trop de bonbons aujourd'hui.
en: You are eating too many candies today.
ipa: /ty mɑ̃ʒ tʁo də bɔ̃bɔ̃ oʒuʁdɥi/
notes: Aujourd'hui is itself a frozen elision of au jour de hui and must be written as one word with an apostrophe.

fr: Les voisins cuisinent un plat traditionnel pour la fête.
en: The neighbors are cooking a traditional dish for the celebration.
ipa: /le vwazɛ̃ kɥizin œ̃ pla tʁadisjɔnɛl puʁ la fɛt/
notes: Cuisinent sounds just like the singular cuisine, so only les voisins shows it is plural.

fr: Je bois un jus d'orange le matin.
en: I drink orange juice in the morning.
ipa: /ʒə bwa œ̃ ʒy dɔʁɑ̃ʒ lə matɛ̃/
notes: Un and matin both end in nasal vowels that hide any separate n sound.

fr: Elle a acheté des tomates au marché.
en: She bought tomatoes at the market.
ipa: /ɛl a aʃte de tɔmat o maʁʃe/
notes: The auxiliary a and the preposition à sound identical, only the accent marks the difference.

fr: Nous avons mangé une pizza délicieuse.
en: We ate a delicious pizza.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ mɑ̃ʒe yn pidza delisjøz/
notes: Mangé, manger and mangez are all pronounced the same way, so grammar must decide the ending.

fr: Il va préparer le dîner ce soir.
en: He is going to prepare dinner tonight.
ipa: /il va pʁepaʁe lə dine sə swaʁ/
notes: The final r of the infinitive préparer is never pronounced.

fr: Nous allons faire les courses ce matin.
en: We are going to do the grocery shopping this morning.
ipa: /nuz‿alɔ̃ fɛʁ le kuʁs sə matɛ̃/
notes: Nous allons links with a z liaison before the vowel of allons.

fr: Elle a mis la table avant le repas.
en: She set the table before the meal.
ipa: /ɛl a mi la tabl avɑ̃ lə ʁəpa/
notes: The past participle mis ends in a silent s that is often forgotten in dictation.

fr: Ils ont mangé toutes les crêpes.
en: They ate all the crepes.
ipa: /ilz‿ɔ̃ mɑ̃ʒe tut le kʁɛp/
notes: Ont and on sound exactly the same, so only context shows which one is meant.

fr: On a préparé un gâteau pour son anniversaire.
en: We made a cake for his birthday.
ipa: /ɔ̃ a pʁepaʁe œ̃ gato puʁ sɔ̃n‿anivɛʁsɛʁ/
notes: On is easily confused with ont since both are pronounced the same nasal sound.

fr: Où as-tu acheté ce fromage?
en: Where did you buy this cheese?
ipa: /u a ty aʃte sə fʁɔmaʒ/
notes: Où, meaning where, and ou, meaning or, are pronounced identically, only the accent separates them.

fr: Tu vas éplucher les pommes de terre.
en: You are going to peel the potatoes.
ipa: /ty va eplyʃe le pɔm də tɛʁ/
notes: The final r of éplucher stays silent, as in every -er infinitive.

fr: Elle a fait cuire les pâtes dix minutes.
en: She cooked the pasta for ten minutes.
ipa: /ɛl a fɛ kɥiʁ le pat di minyt/
notes: The irregular past participle fait ends in a silent t.

fr: Nous avons goûté la sauce avant de la servir.
en: We tasted the sauce before serving it.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ gute la sos avɑ̃ də la sɛʁviʁ/
notes: Goûté still carries the circumflex accent from goûter, even in the past participle.

fr: Les enfants ont bu tout le jus d'orange.
en: The children drank all the orange juice.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ ɔ̃ by tu lə ʒy dɔʁɑ̃ʒ/
notes: Enfants liaises into ont with a hidden z sound that must still be written as two words.

fr: Elle va couper les carottes en rondelles.
en: She is going to cut the carrots into rounds.
ipa: /ɛl va kupe le kaʁɔt ɑ̃ ʁɔ̃dɛl/
notes: Like all -er infinitives, couper ends in a completely silent r.

fr: J'ai lavé la salade avant de la manger.
en: I washed the salad before eating it.
ipa: /ʒe lave la salad avɑ̃ də la mɑ̃ʒe/
notes: Lavé, laver and lavez all sound the same, so the ending must be chosen by grammar, not by ear.

fr: Nous avons acheté des pommes et des poires.
en: We bought apples and pears.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃z‿aʃte de pɔm e de pwaʁ/
notes: Avons acheté chains two liaisons in a row that are easy to miss in fast speech.

fr: Il a versé l'huile dans la poêle chaude.
en: He poured the oil into the hot pan.
ipa: /il a vɛʁse lɥil dɑ̃ la pwal ʃod/
notes: La huile is unpronounceable, so it becomes l'huile before the vowel sound.

fr: Elle a préparé la soupe qu'elle a servie chaude.
en: She made the soup she served hot.
ipa: /ɛl a pʁepaʁe la sup kɛl a sɛʁvi ʃod/
notes: Servie is pronounced exactly like servi, but the silent added e agrees with the feminine soupe.

fr: On va manger dans la cuisine ce soir.
en: We are going to eat in the kitchen tonight.
ipa: /ɔ̃ va mɑ̃ʒe dɑ̃ la kɥizin sə swaʁ/
notes: On here is easy to confuse with ont since both share the same nasal sound.

fr: Les invités sont arrivés avant le dîner.
en: The guests arrived before dinner.
ipa: /lez‿ɛ̃vite sɔ̃t‿aʁive avɑ̃ lə dine/
notes: With être, arrivés adds a silent s to agree with the plural invités.

fr: Elle a coupé les légumes qu'elle a lavés ce matin.
en: She cut the vegetables she washed this morning.
ipa: /ɛl a kupe le legym kɛl a lave sə matɛ̃/
notes: Lavés sounds identical to lavé, but the silent s agrees with the plural légumes.

fr: Il faut que nous mangions des légumes variés chaque jour.
en: We must eat varied vegetables every day.
ipa: /il fo kə nu mɑ̃ʒjɔ̃ de legym vaʁje ʃak ʒuʁ/
notes: Before the ending -ions, -ger verbs like manger drop the extra e since the following i already softens the g.

fr: Je ne pense pas que ce plat soit trop épicé.
en: I do not think this dish is too spicy.
ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sə pla swa tʁo epise/
notes: Ce, meaning this, and se, the reflexive pronoun, are pronounced exactly the same way.

fr: Ces épices viennent du marché, mais ses habitudes culinaires ont changé.
en: These spices come from the market, but her cooking habits have changed.
ipa: /sez‿episɛ vjɛn dy maʁʃe mɛ sez‿abityd kylinɛʁ ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe/
notes: Ces and ses sound completely identical, so only grammar tells them apart.

fr: C'est la recette que ma grand-mère préférait.
en: This is the recipe my grandmother preferred.
ipa: /sɛ la ʁəsɛt kə ma gʁɑ̃mɛʁ pʁefeʁɛ/
notes: C'est sounds the same as ces and ses, so the apostrophe is the only visual clue.

fr: Quel plat préfères-tu pour le dîner de ce soir?
en: Which dish do you prefer for dinner tonight?
ipa: /kɛl pla pʁefɛʁ ty puʁ lə dine də sə swaʁ/
notes: Quel and quelle sound identical, so the ending must match the noun's gender in writing.

fr: Quelle sauce accompagne le mieux ce poisson grillé?
en: Which sauce goes best with this grilled fish?
ipa: /kɛl sos akɔ̃paɲ lə mjø sə pwasɔ̃ gʁije/
notes: Quelle sounds exactly like quel, so only the feminine noun sauce shows the correct spelling.

fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, elle continue à préparer le repas.
en: Although it is late, she keeps preparing the meal.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa taʁ ɛl kɔ̃tiny a pʁepaʁe lə ʁəpa/
notes: The subjunctive soit ends in a silent t that is easy to drop by mistake.

fr: Il faudrait que vous ajoutiez un peu plus de sel.
en: You should add a little more salt.
ipa: /il fodʁɛ kə vuz‿aʒutje œ̃ pø ply də sɛl/
notes: The ending -iez is pronounced yé, which is easy to confuse with the simpler -ez ending.

fr: Elle doute que ce dessert soit vraiment sans sucre.
en: She doubts this dessert is really sugar free.
ipa: /ɛl dut kə sə desɛʁ swa vʁɛmɑ̃ sɑ̃ sykʁ/
notes: Sans sounds identical to sang and cent, so only context fixes the spelling.

fr: Les invités, bien qu'ils aient déjà mangé, reprennent du gâteau.
en: The guests, although they already ate, take more cake.
ipa: /lez‿ɛ̃vite bjɛ̃ kilz‿ɛ deʒa mɑ̃ʒe ʁəpʁɛn dy gato/
notes: The subjunctive aient is pronounced just like est, with the whole ending staying silent.

fr: Ce cuisinier ne se souvient plus de la recette exacte.
en: This cook no longer remembers the exact recipe.
ipa: /sə kɥizinje nə sə suvjɛ̃ ply də la ʁəsɛt ɛgzakt/
notes: Ce and se appear together here and sound completely identical.

fr: Mes parents pensent que ces légumes sont meilleurs que les surgelés.
en: My parents think these vegetables are better than frozen ones.
ipa: /me paʁɑ̃ pɑ̃s kə se legym sɔ̃ mɛjœʁ kə le syʁʒəle/
notes: Ces is a homophone of ses and c'est, easily mixed up while writing quickly.

fr: Il semble que les enfants aient adoré le repas.
en: It seems the children loved the meal.
ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃z‿ɛ adɔʁe lə ʁəpa/
notes: The liaison before aient sounds just like the liaison before ont, so the two are easy to confuse when writing.

fr: Je voudrais que tu choisisses un dessert pour ce soir.
en: I would like you to choose a dessert for tonight.
ipa: /ʒə vudʁɛ kə ty ʃwazis œ̃ desɛʁ puʁ sə swaʁ/
notes: The subjunctive choisisses is pronounced exactly like the indicative choisis, with the extra letters staying silent.

fr: Nous avons besoin d'un grand chef pour organiser ce banquet.
en: We need a great chef to organize this banquet.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ bəzwɛ̃ dœ̃ gʁɑ̃ ʃɛf puʁ ɔʁganize sə bɑ̃kɛ/
notes: De un is never said aloud, so it becomes d'un before the vowel.

fr: Ce dessert paraît trop sucré pour certains invités.
en: This dessert seems too sweet for some guests.
ipa: /sə desɛʁ paʁɛ tʁo sykʁe puʁ sɛʁtɛ̃z‿ɛ̃vite/
notes: Certains and invités both carry nasal vowels that hide any separate n sound before the liaison.

fr: Les grands chefs insistent pour que les ingrédients soient frais.
en: Great chefs insist that the ingredients be fresh.
ipa: /le gʁɑ̃ ʃɛfz‿ɛ̃sist puʁ kə lez‿ɛ̃gʁedjɑ̃ swat fʁɛ/
notes: The liaison after plural chefs is easy to mistake for the sound of a singular chef alone.

fr: Elle a l'habitude de goûter chaque plat avant qu'il ne soit servi.
en: She usually tastes every dish before it is served.
ipa: /ɛl a labityd də gute ʃak pla avɑ̃ kil nə swa sɛʁvi/
notes: La habitude cannot be pronounced, so it elides to l'habitude.

fr: Ses amis pensent que ce restaurant mérite trois étoiles.
en: Her friends think this restaurant deserves three stars.
ipa: /sez‿ami pɑ̃s kə sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ meʁit tʁwaz‿etwal/
notes: Ses sounds the same as ce and c'est, so only grammar reveals the right spelling.

fr: Il vaut mieux que nous réservions une table avant huit heures.
en: It is better that we reserve a table before eight o'clock.
ipa: /il vo mjø kə nu ʁezɛʁvjɔ̃ yn tabl avɑ̃ ɥit‿œʁ/
notes: The t of huit is silent alone but reappears in liaison before the vowel of heures.

fr: C'est étonnant que ces enfants aiment autant les épinards.
en: It is surprising that these children like spinach so much.
ipa: /sɛt‿etɔnɑ̃ kə sez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ ɛm otɑ̃ lez‿epinaʁ/
notes: C'est and ces are pronounced the same way, distinguishable only by their spelling and role.

fr: Quelles épices utilises-tu pour ce curry maison?
en: Which spices do you use for this homemade curry?
ipa: /kɛlz‿episɛ ytiliz ty puʁ sə kyʁi mɛzɔ̃/
notes: Quelles épices links with a z liaison that must still be spelled as two separate words.

fr: Bien que ce gâteau soit simple, il plaît à tout le monde.
en: Although this cake is simple, everyone likes it.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə sə gato swa sɛ̃pl il plɛ a tu lə mɔ̃d/
notes: Plaît keeps a circumflex accent on the i, a silent spelling detail carried over from plaire.

fr: Nous doutons que ses économies suffisent pour ce restaurant étoilé.
en: We doubt her savings are enough for this starred restaurant.
ipa: /nu dutɔ̃ kə sez‿ekɔnɔmi syfiz puʁ sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ etwale/
notes: Ses is a classic homophone trap, sounding identical to ce and c'est.
